clarification.Should the architect keep this draft's e: Keep the draft structure exactly as-is — 2 modules with 3 lessons each (6 lessons total). Do NOT merge, split, drop, or add lessons. Refine titles and slugs only.
clarification.Which Python ML stack should examples ta: Pure PyTorch (no Lightning/HuggingFace wrappers). NumPy is the reference comparison.
clarification.Should examples assume GPU access?: No — every exercise must run CPU-only. GPU/CUDA is discussed conceptually only.

draftStructure.courseDescription: A focused, hands-on introduction to PyTorch for engineers already comfortable with Python and NumPy. Two compact modules: the tensor + autograd foundation, then a minimal training loop end-to-end.

lessons.title: Tensors vs NumPy Arrays
lessons.summary: Compare torch.Tensor with numpy.ndarray, learn dtype/device/shape, and convert between the two safely.

lessons.title: Autograd Basics: requires_grad and backward()
lessons.summary: Build a tiny computational graph, call .backward(), and inspect .grad on leaf tensors.

lessons.title: Devices and Moving Tensors to the GPU
lessons.summary: Detect CUDA availability, move tensors with .to(device), and avoid the most common CPU/GPU mismatch errors.

lessons.title: Defining a Model with nn.Module
lessons.summary: Subclass nn.Module, register layers in __init__, and implement forward() for a small MLP.

lessons.title: Loss Functions and Optimizers
lessons.summary: Pick a loss (MSE / CrossEntropy), construct an optimizer (SGD / Adam), and understand zero_grad / step.

lessons.title: Putting It Together: A Full Training Step
lessons.summary: Write a single training iteration end-to-end: forward → loss → backward → step, and explain what each line does.
